findings.title: template_sha256 describes the bytes read at scan time, but the prompt is rendered from a later re-read of the file
findings.detail: `persona_defs._check_template` hashes the template bytes while validating. `Persona.template` re-reads `template_file` from disk every time `build_prompt` runs. If the file changes between the registry scan and rendering, `Persona.declared["template_sha256"]` (and the placeholder check) no longer describe the prompt that was sent. Today the hash is only displayed, but it is offered as the identity of the template, and Pipeline A3 may record or trust it. The placeholder confinement from SPEC-0371 has the same TOCTOU, so this is not new risk, but the new field claims more than it can guarantee.
findings.trigger: The main-checkout `.nw/personas/security_reviewer.md` is edited (e.g. by a `git pull` on main) between `get_persona(...)` in `build_request` and `build_prompt(p, ctx)`, or between `nw personas show` and a later run.

findings.title: A declared model id with a trailing newline passes validation
findings.detail: `check_declared_keys` accepts a model if `MODEL_RE.match(model)` succeeds. `MODEL_RE` ends in `$`, which also matches just before a final `\n`, so a quoted YAML value such as `model: "claude-opus-4-1\n"` validates. It then reaches `RunRequest.model` and the claude argv unchanged and fails at run time instead of at `nw personas validate`. The regex already exists in profiles.py; a definition file is only a new place for such a value to come from. `fullmatch` (or `\Z`) would close it.

waived.waive_reason: The test plan checks that queue.py, profiles.py and divergence.py are untouched with `git diff --stat main`, and the reviewer says that diff touches none of them. An automated test for this is not required.

waived.title: "Unchanged" builtin tables are checked only by membership, not against a baseline
waived.waive_reason: The diff does not edit the builtin tables, and existing registry tests pin them. The membership checks already cover the declared-name leak that AC9 cares about.

waived.title: Invalid run-setting values are tested only on the reviewer role and mostly through one validator
waived.waive_reason: Both validators share one helper, and the multi-fault file already covers every key through both. Extra parametrization would add little.

waived.title: template_sha256 describes the bytes read at scan time, but the prompt is rendered from a later re-read of the file
waived.waive_reason: The reviewer says this has the same TOCTOU as the SPEC-0371 placeholder confinement. The hash is display-only for now, and any use of it for identity belongs to Pipeline A3.

waived.title: build_request computes the review flag inline instead of calling is_reviewer as the Design says
waived.waive_reason: The deviation is documented in As shipped and pinned by a test. It gives the same answer with one registry scan. Where to put the predicate is a style choice.

waived.title: "Diff does not touch queue.py/profiles.py/divergence.py" is a manual check
waived.waive_reason: The spec explicitly makes AC9's not-touched check a manual `git diff --stat`. An automated test would be out of scope.

sizing.rationale: Ten acceptance criteria across persona_registry.py, persona_defs.py, personas.py (Persona, build_request, build_prompt, new is_reviewer/declared_settings), the `nw personas` CLI and the capability doc. It is high-end rather than cost-effective because it changes run-request construction and forces read-only/dontAsk permissions, although the queue and the builtin path stay untouched.

findings.title: build_request computes the review flag inline instead of calling is_reviewer as the Design says
findings.detail: Design §build_request says `review=is_reviewer(persona, project_root)`. The shipped code uses `persona in REVIEWER_PERSONAS or (p.declared is not None and p.role == "reviewer")` on the persona it has already resolved (personas.py:1003-1004). The answer is the same, and this way the registry is scanned once per request. The deviation is recorded in *As shipped* and pinned by test_build_request_resolves_the_declared_registry_once. Because the predicate now lives in two places, is_reviewer and build_request could drift apart later.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally move the predicate into one private helper, e.g. `_is_review_persona(name, p)`, and call it from both is_reviewer (after its registry lookup) and build_request, so the rule is written once.
findings.acceptance: test_is_reviewer and test_build_request_declared_reviewer still pass, and grep finds the reviewer-role predicate in a single place.

ac_assessment.evidence: persona_registry.check_declared_keys validates model (MODEL_ALIASES/MODEL_RE), effort (EFFORTS) and max_budget_usd (_is_budget: finite, >0, not bool). validate_persona_doc refuses the keys in a builtin layer with 'allowed only in a user or project definition'. Tests: test_settings_keys_valid (3 roles), test_settings_keys_invalid (gpt4, 'claude', 3, extreme, list, 0, inf, nan, -1.5, true, '2.0') each asserting file:key prefix, test_declared_keys_refused_in_a_builtin_definition.

check_declared_keys refuses required/when on implementer/triager ('only allowed for role reviewer'), checks required is a bool, when is a mapping, its keys are paths/labels only, and each value is a non-empty list of non-blank strings. declared_values defaults to required True and when {}. Tests: test_routing_keys_valid_for_reviewer, test_routing_keys_reviewer_only_bad_shapes (null, list, scalar, unknown key, empty, non-string, blank), test_routing_keys_reviewer_only, test_declared_mapping_defaults.

The diff touches no queue.py, profiles.py or divergence.py (only cli_personas, persona_defs, persona_registry, personas, docs and tests). Persona.declared defaults to None for builtins. test_inert checks PERSONAS/REVIEWER_PERSONAS/ADOPT_REGISTRY and that resolve_profile raises for a declared reviewer in reviewers:. test_declared_mapping_defaults asserts every builtin has declared None.

docs/product/capabilities/agentic.md gains a 'Declared personas (SPEC-0371, SPEC-0394)' subsection with the security_reviewer example, the role table, the new keys and their layering, nw personas list|show|validate, and the bold statement that the queue does not run them yet.

findings.title: "Unchanged" builtin tables are checked only by membership, not against a baseline
findings.detail: test_inert checks that PERSONAS equals the persona_defs/*.yaml stems and that the declared name is absent from PERSONAS, REVIEWER_PERSONAS and ADOPT_REGISTRY. It never compares REVIEWER_PERSONAS or ADOPT_REGISTRY to a pinned expected value, so a change that dropped or added a builtin reviewer or adopt entry would still pass. The diff does not edit these tables, and existing registry tests probably pin them, so the risk is low.

findings.title: Invalid run-setting values are tested only on the reviewer role and mostly through one validator
findings.detail: test_settings_keys_invalid runs only on role reviewer, and only through validate_persona_defs. The registry validator (persona_registry.validate_persona_doc) sees bad model, effort and budget values only through the one multi-fault file. That file covers each key, and the helper is shared, so the gap is small. A parametrized check of entry.errors per bad value, and one implementer or triager case, would pin AC3's "same messages" claim for each rule.

findings.title: "Diff does not touch queue.py/profiles.py/divergence.py" is a manual check
findings.detail: The spec says this is checked by hand with `git diff --stat main`, which is acceptable. No automated test guards it.

findings.title: template_sha256 describes the bytes read at scan time, but the prompt is rendered from a later re-read of the file
findings.detail: `persona_defs._check_template` hashes the template bytes while validating. `Persona.template` re-reads `template_file` from disk every time `build_prompt` runs. If the file changes between the registry scan and rendering, `Persona.declared["template_sha256"]` (and the placeholder check) no longer describe the prompt that was sent. Today the hash is only displayed, but it is offered as the identity of the template, and Pipeline A3 may record or trust it. The placeholder confinement from SPEC-0371 has the same TOCTOU, so this is not new risk, but the new field claims more than it can guarantee.
findings.trigger: The main-checkout `.nw/personas/security_reviewer.md` is edited (e.g. by a `git pull` on main) between `get_persona(...)` in `build_request` and `build_prompt(p, ctx)`, or between `nw personas show` and a later run.

findings.title: A declared model id with a trailing newline passes validation
findings.detail: `check_declared_keys` accepts a model if `MODEL_RE.match(model)` succeeds. `MODEL_RE` ends in `$`, which also matches just before a final `\n`, so a quoted YAML value such as `model: "claude-opus-4-1\n"` validates. It then reaches `RunRequest.model` and the claude argv unchanged and fails at run time instead of at `nw personas validate`. The regex already exists in profiles.py; a definition file is only a new place for such a value to come from. `fullmatch` (or `\Z`) would close it.

waived.title: build_request computes the review flag inline instead of calling is_reviewer as the Design says
waived.detail:
Design §build_request says `review=is_reviewer(persona, project_root)`. The shipped code uses `persona in REVIEWER_PERSONAS or (p.declared is not None and p.role == "reviewer")` on the persona it has already resolved (personas.py:1003-1004). The answer is the same, and this way the registry is scanned once per request. The deviation is recorded in *As shipped* and pinned by test_build_request_resolves_the_declared_registry_once. Because the predicate now lives in two places, is_reviewer and build_request could drift apart later.
Fix: Optionally move the predicate into one private helper, e.g. `_is_review_persona(name, p)`, and call it from both is_reviewer (after its registry lookup) and build_request, so the rule is written once.
Done when: test_is_reviewer and test_build_request_declared_reviewer still pass, and grep finds the reviewer-role predicate in a single place.
waived.reason: The deviation is documented in As shipped and pinned by a test. It gives the same answer with one registry scan. Where to put the predicate is a style choice.

review_carry.title: template_sha256 is of the validated bytes, not of the template the prompt renders
review_carry.detail:
_check_template hashes and placeholder-checks the bytes it reads during the scan. Persona.template re-reads the file from disk when the prompt is built. The recorded sha256 (and the role-placeholder confinement) can therefore describe different content than what the agent actually received, which weakens the sha as provenance once A3 records it. The spec defines the sha this way, so this is hardening only.
trigger: The template file is edited after load_registry and before build_prompt reads `p.template`.
review_carry.waive_reason: The spec defines template_sha256 as the hash of the bytes read during validation. The reviewer calls it hardening only, and the spec does not ask for it.

review_carry.title: Output section lists `trigger`, which the Design's field list does not include
review_carry.detail:
output_section derives the optional finding fields from reviewer_schema, so it lists `detail`, `trigger`, `files` and `lines`. The Design names only `detail`, `files` and `lines`. The 'As shipped' section records this deviation, and it follows the spec's own rule that the section is read from the enforced schema.
Fix: No code change. Keep the 'As shipped' note, or add `trigger` to the Design's list in the spec so the two agree.
Done when: The spec Design and the generated `## Output` text name the same optional fields.
review_carry.waive_reason: The output section is derived from the enforced schema, and the spec's 'As shipped' section records the extra `trigger` field. Not a defect.
